To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the feedback laws proposed are effective in shaping the output traffic to the declared TSpec, and the proposed analytical framework is effective in evaluating the impact of the choice of feedback laws on the perceived image quality.
the proposed feedback law is able to maintain a low marking probability and a low quantization distortion.
the feedback law based on the encoder output buffer state can be used to shape the traffic to the desired Tspec while keeping an acceptable image quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of feedback laws for MPEG encoders which provide an efficient traffic shaping capability while maintaining an acceptable quality of service.
a novel feedback law which is able to provide a constant quantization distortion, and which is able to shape the traffic according to a declared Tspec.
the design of a feedback law which provides an efficient Tspec shaping while maintaining the quality of the perceived images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed analytical framework can provide the designer with an effective tool for evaluating the performance of the addressed MPEG video traffic shapers in terms of marking probability and quantization distortion.

the use of the proposed analytical tool allows to evaluate quantization distortion and marking probability for a large class of feedback laws, and thus to select the one providing the best trade-off between these two parameters.
the proposed feedback law provides a very efficient traffic shaping, with a low quantization distortion, and with a very low marking probability, even when the traffic characteristics are tight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a proper choice of the quantizer scale factor, which is a function of the encoder output queue length, can provide a good tradeoff between the two performance metrics.

it is possible to design a feedback law which provides a traffic source with a constant marking probability while maintaining the quantization distortion below a given threshold, thus providing an acceptable perceived image Quality.
we have proposed a new feedback algorithm for the MPEG video source, which is based on the use of the encoder buffer occupancy to control the output bit rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of feedback laws based on a single quantizer scale parameter is not suitable for Tspec compliant transmission of MPEG video over an intserv network.
a simple feedback law can provide an acceptable tradeoff between the two performance metrics.

the proposed analytical framework can be used to evaluate and compare the performance of feedback laws which can be used to shape the output MPEG traffic according to the Tspec declared to the network.
